texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Nitesh Kumar S/o Sh. Vidya Sagar, suffered grievous MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 2 Of 22 BK injury. An application u/s 166 (1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant Nitesh Kumar. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 05.04.2018, petitioner was coming to UP Gate from Dabur Chawk on Motorcycle bearing No. DL-3STP-4737 and when he reached near UP Gate, then Honda Amaze car No. UK-07BH- 2018(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle no.1) struck the Alto car bearing no. DL-7CN-4570(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle no.2) and the said Alto car dashed against the motorcycle of petitioner. Due to the accident, petitioner received serious injuries. It is averred that accident occurred due to sole negligence of the driver of offending vehicle no.1. After accident, petitioner was removed to Max hospital, Delhi and later shifted to Holy Family hospital, Okhla where he remained admitted from 05.04.2018 to 11.04.2018. 3. An FIR no. 0779/21 dated 06.04.2018 was registered u/s 279,338,427 of IPC at PS Indrapuram, District Ghaziabad and the matter was investigated. After investigation a charge sheet was filed before Ld. MM. 4. As the accident allegedly occurred on account of striking of offending vehicle no.1 into offending vehicle no.2 that hit the motorcycle of the petitioner, driver, owner and insurance company of both the involved cars i.e. UK-07BWS-2018 as well as vehicle no. DL-7CN-4570 were impleaded as parties to the case. As such, Respondent no.1 and Respondent no.2 are owner and driver of offending vehicle no.1 which is insured with Respondent no.3 while Respondent no.4 is driver-cum-owner of offending vehicle no.2,insured with Respondent no.5. MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 3 Of 22 BK Nitesh Kumar vs Piyush Kumar Goel on 5 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77958717/ 2 5. Pursuant to issuance of notice, Respondent no.1,2,3 and 5 appeared. Respondent no.4 was through publication despite which he failed to appear and was proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 07.09.2021. 6. Reply/ Written statements were filed on behalf of Respondent no.3 and 5. As per reply/written statement filed by Respondent no.3, allegations of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle have been denied. It is pleaded that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving by offending vehicle no.2. It is further pleaded that the petitioner who was negligent while driving his motorcycle. However, it admitted that the offending vehicle no.1 was insured with Respondent no.3 on the date of accident. 8. Respondent no. 5 has denied its liability by filing reply/written statement and pleading that the accident occurred due to sole rash and negligence of the driver of offending vehicle no.1. Respondent no.5 has also pleaded contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner as the petitioner is alleged to have been driving without a driving licence. It is, however, not denied that the offending vehicle no.2 was insured with Respondent no.5 as on the date of accident. 9. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 07.09.2021. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 05.04.2018 due to rash and composite negligence of vehicle bearing no.UK07BS2018 driven by R-2,owned by R-1 & insured with R-3 and vehicle bearing no.DL7CN4570 driven & owned by R-4 and insured with R-5? OPP. MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 4 Of 22 BK 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 10. Thereafter, evidence was led through local commissioner, by the petitioner by examining petitioner Sh. Nitesh Kumar as PW-1 and Sh. Durgesh Kumar, Record clerk from Holy Family Hospital as PW-2. PW-1/petitioner Sh. Nitesh Kumar led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A and relied upon copy of FIR, Map, chargesheet & MLC is Mark-A (colly page 1 to 30), original Medical bills as Ex.PW-1/1(colly), Aadhar card and PAN card of petitioner as Ex.PW-1/2(OSR), copy of Educational documents like High School, Intermediate Certificate, Diploma in Mechanical Engineering as Mark-B(colly). PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.3/Oriental insurance company and Respondent no.5/ICICI Lombard Company Ltd. Sh. Durgesh Kumar was examined as PW-2. He was a summoned witness. He relied upon authority letter as Ex.PW- 2/A and deposed that petitioner was admitted in Holy Family hospital from 05.04.2018 to 11.04.2018. He also relied upon discharge summary of petitioner as Ex.PW-2/B(colly), true copy of medical bills as Ex.PW-2/C(colly). He was duly cross- examined by Nitesh Kumar vs Piyush Kumar Goel on 5 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77958717/ 3 Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.3/Oriental insurance company and Respondent no.5/ICICI Lombard Company Ltd. 11. Respondents did not lead any evidence despite opportunity. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 14. In the present case, petitioner/injured has specifically deposed that on 05.04.2018, he was coming to UP Gate, Ghaziabad from Dabur Chowk on his motorcycle bearing no. DL-3STP-4737. At around 4 pm, when he reached near UP Gate, offending vehicle i.e. Honda Amaze bearing no. UK-07BH-2018 coming from Delhi side, dashed into an Alto car bearing no. DL- 7CN-4570 and the said Alto car, consequently dashed into his motorcycle. Due to the accident, victim's motorcycle was damaged and he sustained injuries (i.e. fracture in right knee and MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 6 Of 22 BK right shoulder). He deposed that he was admitted in Max hospital, Delhi and later shifted to Holy Family hospital where he remained admitted from 05.04.2018 to 11.04.2018 and continued to take treatment after his discharge. He deposed that he cannot run or do any work due to the injuries sustained as a result of the accident. He deposed that he was working in Innovative Servers Pvt. Ltd., Rohini at the salary of Rs.15,000/- p.m. He deposed that he had spent Rs.6,50,000/- towards his treatment/special diet, conveyance and other expenses and also suffered financial loss of Rs.15,000/-p.m. as he was unfit for his service. 15. On being cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for Respondent no.3 and 5, PW-1 reiterated the facts as mentioned in his examination-in-chief. He admitted that he did not file any disability certificate nor salary certificate of earning Rs.15,000/- p.m. He also admitted that he has not filed any documents that he has spent Rs.6.5 lacs on his treatment, special diet and conveyance, however, volunteered told that he has filed medical bills of Rs.1,29,865/- towards treatment. He admitted that after accident he joined TATA AIG on 24.12.2018 and getting Rs.17,000/- per month and also admitted that he is presently working with HDFC Ergo Company as a surveyor and getting salary of Rs.39,000/- p.m. Further, in his cross-examination by Respondent no.5, PW-1 admitted that the Nitesh Kumar vs Piyush Kumar Goel on 5 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77958717/ 4 accident occurred due to sole rash and negligence of the driver of Honda Amaze Car bearing no. UK-7BH-2018. 16. From the evidence so recorded and the nature of suggestions put by Respondent no.3 and 5, it is apparent that the accident was caused due to sole negligence on the part of the MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 7 Of 22 BK driver of offending vehicle no.1 which hit the Alto car(offending vehicle no.2) causing it to dash against the motorcycle of injured. There is nothing to show that despite such impact caused due to the accident by offending vehicle no.1, vehicle no.2 could have avoided the accident withi motorcycle of petitioner. Facts make it abundantly evident that vehicle no.2 was not at fault in as much as its accident with the vehicle of the petitioner was only an impact caused due to dashing of offending vehicle no.1 due to rash and negligence of driver of such offending vehicle no.1. Thus, it is proved that it is solely offending vehicle no.1 which was responsible for the accident caused due to rash and negligent driving. Driver, owner and insurance company of such offending vehicle no.1 accordingly hold responsibility to compensate the injured while driver, owner and insurance company of offending vehicle no.2 stands exonerated of liability to compensate the victim. Further, MLC Ex.PW-2/B reflects that the injured was diagnosed with close displaced fracture shaft in right tibia. Medical record/discharge summary also reveals that the injured underwent surgical/invasive procedure. Thus, the injury sustained by the petitioner is proved to be grievous in nature. 17. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge sheet against Respondent no.1 under Section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal. 18. No respondent witness entered into the witness box to oppose the case of injured/petitioner. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner/ claimant/applicant and against the respondents. Accordingly, Issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the petitioner.
texts.arguments: In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 8 Of 22 BK negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 24. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 10 Of 22 BK would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 24.7. 30. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. In compliance of directions issued vide order dated 16.11.2021 by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Writ Petition Civil No.534/2020 titled as Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Union of India the award amount shall be deposited with State Bank of India, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT SAVING ACCOUNT No. 00000042706875094, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir in the prescribed format i.e. MCOP Number on the file of (Claims Tribunal Name) Date of award, Compensation Amount, Income Tax Deduction at Source, Bank Transaction Reference No./Unique Transaction Reference (UTR) Number. On such deposits being made, the insurance company shall submit a letter to the Nazir of this Tribunal enclosing a copy of the said MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 16 Of 22 BK bank advice, in prescribed format as above, as per which the deposit made to the bank account of this Tribunal, to enable this Tribunal to keep tab on the deposits made and the MCOPs for which they were made. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 36. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the MACT NO: 254/19 Nitesh Kumar v. Piyush Kumar Goel P.No. 18 Of 22 BK amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. whereas in the guideline Nos.
